title: 2.1.3 Boolean Operations
description: Use union, subtract, and intersect to combine and cut 2D shapes.

steps.title: Import booleans
steps.instructions: Add `booleans` to your destructured import: `const { primitives, transforms, booleans } = require('@jscad/modeling')`
hints: booleans gives you union(), subtract(), and intersect().

steps.title: Use union to combine shapes
steps.instructions: Create two overlapping shapes and combine them with `booleans.union(shape1, shape2)`.
hints: Union merges shapes into one. The result is the combined outline of both.
Make sure shapes overlap: union of non-overlapping shapes just groups them.

steps.title: Use subtract to cut shapes
steps.instructions: Use `booleans.subtract(baseShape, cutterShape)` to cut one shape out of another.
hints: Order matters! subtract(A, B) cuts B out of A.
Try: subtract a circle from a rectangle to make a shape with a round hole.

steps.title: Use intersect to keep overlap
steps.instructions: Use `booleans.intersect(shape1, shape2)` to keep only the area where both shapes overlap.
hints: Intersect keeps only the shared region.
If shapes don't overlap, intersect returns nothing.

requirements.title: Use at least two primitives
requirements.description: Create shapes from at least 2 different primitive types
